claim: Saturn's average density, about 687 kg/m3, is less than water's, because it is mostly hydrogen and helium spread over a huge volume.

beats.caption: 95x Earth's mass. Density: 687 kg/m³.
beats.vo: Saturn has about 95 times Earth's mass. But its average density is only 687 kilograms per cubic meter. Water is about 1,000.

beats.caption: Mostly hydrogen and helium
beats.vo: Saturn is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the two lightest elements. And it is huge, with about 760 times Earth's volume. So that mass is spread very thin.

beats.caption: About 9x wider than Earth
beats.vo: Saturn is about nine times wider than Earth, so you would need a bathtub far bigger than our whole planet.

beats.caption: The only planet less dense than water
beats.vo: That makes Saturn the only planet in our solar system less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub, it would float. Which planet would you drop in next?

sources.text: NASA Science, Saturn Facts: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ (mostly hydrogen and helium; only planet with average density less than water)

NASA NSSDC Saturn Fact Sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturnfact.html (mean density 687 kg/m3; mass 95.16x Earth; volume 763.59x Earth) Equatorial radius 9.4x Earth's, volumetric mean radius 9.14x.
